# Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers — facts

## How it works

- [statement] Duplicate-safe handling is required for both the managed Trigger baseline and a Debezium replacement pipeline: Atlas documents duplicates after progress-recording failures or unordered recovery, while Debezium documents replay from the last recorded offset after a crash. These sources do not promise exactly-once external side effects. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers · also: https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/connectors/mongodb.html, https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/mongodb.html
- [statement] Atlas Auto-Resume after a missing resume token skips missed events from token loss until completion of the resume process. Manually starting a suspended Trigger without a token likewise listens only for new events. A replacement recovery procedure must distinguish replay from deliberately restarting after a gap. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/database-triggers.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers
- [statement] Keep checkpoint positions moving during quiet periods: Debezium recommends heartbeat messages when only excluded collections change, because otherwise offsets may not be committed and oplog rotation can prevent restart. The MongoDB driver specification caches `postBatchResumeToken` from empty batches and requires a way for users to obtain updated tokens without waiting for a change document. (medium confidence) — https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/mongodb.html · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/change-streams/change-streams.md
- [statement] Review projections when porting Trigger event handling: Atlas permits explicitly excluding `_id` from the event passed to a Trigger Function, while the native change-stream manual says not to modify or remove the event `_id` because it is the resume token. Copying a Trigger projection unchanged can therefore break the native consumer's resumability. Atlas also requires an inclusive Project Expression that includes `operationType`. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/database-triggers.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changeStreams.md
- [statement] Preserving ordered Trigger behavior requires serial completion of event handlers: ordered Triggers wait for previous Functions to finish, whereas unordered Triggers may execute in parallel without execution-order guarantees. MongoDB warns that long-running ordered handlers can lag until events fall off the oplog. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/database-triggers.md
- [statement] Scheduled Triggers execute logic on a defined schedule, whereas native change streams are restricted to database events. A change-stream consumer alone therefore does not replace the clock-based invocation of a Scheduled Trigger; the exit design needs a scheduling mechanism as well. This replacement requirement is an architectural inference from the documented event boundaries. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/scheduled-triggers.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changeStreams.md
- [statement] Translate event filters and projections explicitly: Atlas Match Expression filters which events fire a Trigger, and Project Expression selects event fields. Native change streams support filtering and transforming notifications through the aggregation framework. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/database-triggers.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changeStreams.md
- [statement] For scheduled replacement, preserve the schedule and invocation contract: Atlas runs CRON expressions in UTC, and a Scheduled Trigger passes no arguments to its linked Function. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/scheduled-triggers.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The MongoDB driver specification requires one automatic resume attempt for a resumable change-stream error and forbids automatic resume for other error types. This retry contract is narrower than an unlimited application recovery loop. If the aggregate command used to resume succeeds, the driver must permit later resume attempts to succeed even when no change document arrived between attempts. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/change-streams/change-streams.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers
- [statement] Resume with the same pipeline and options that generated the token. The manual warns that changing them can prevent resumption or harm consistency; the driver specification defines `resumeAfter` as returning entries immediately after the supplied token and returning an error when the token does not exist. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changeStreams.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/change-streams/change-streams.md
- [statement] Token-based recovery requires the corresponding operation to remain in the oplog. `resumeAfter` cannot continue after an invalidate event such as a collection drop or rename; `startAfter` can open a new stream after that invalidate event. Neither option restores history already lost from the oplog. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changeStreams.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers · also: https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/mongodb.html
- [statement] A native consumer needs a supported database topology. The MongoDB manual requires replica sets or sharded clusters using WiredTiger and replica set protocol version 1; the driver specification says change streams cannot be initiated on standalone single-server topologies because they lack an oplog. These deployment prerequisites are distinct from reproducing the Trigger execution service, which remains inherited parent context. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changeStreams.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/change-streams/change-streams.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/database-triggers.md
- [statement] A repository reproduction reports that Meteor 3.5 repeatedly resends a stale `startAfter` token after oplog history loss, producing `ChangeStreamHistoryLost` with error 286 until the application restarts. Its suggested fix clears the token and reruns initial queries to address missed events. This is the repository author's report and proposed repair, not evidence of a released Meteor fix or a universal Atlas defect. (low confidence) — https://github.com/matt-dale/meteor-change-stream-failure-repro/blob/main/README.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers
- [statement] Checkpoint loss and oplog expiry are different recovery cases: MongoDB can resume only while the required operation remains in the oplog. Atlas recommends a minimum oplog window longer than the longest expected interruption. The selected Debezium stable documentation identifies version 3.7: on restart the connector attempts the last oplog position, but if that position was removed, startup can fail depending on `snapshot.mode`. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/database-triggers.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers · also: https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/mongodb.html

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Match full-document semantics, not merely event names. Atlas can attach the latest majority-committed document to update events. Native streams return update deltas by default; `fullDocument: "updateLookup"` retrieves the document as it exists when the stream processes the lookup, rather than necessarily its event-time image. The manual warns that `updateLookup` with a `$match` filter can cause Resume Token Not Found errors during rapid deletions or traffic spikes: deletion can make the lookup return null. It recommends pre- and post-images with `fullDocumentBeforeChange` and `fullDocument` set to `whenAvailable` instead. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/database-triggers.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changeStreams.md
- [statement] The selected Debezium stable documentation identifies version 3.7 and describes a MongoDB change-stream connector that emits events downstream to Kafka topics, rather than a replacement function runtime. Its `when_needed` snapshot mode snapshots when topic offsets cannot be detected or a recorded offset names a log position unavailable on the server. The separately selected unversioned page explicitly labels itself unreleased; that page alone does not establish released-product applicability. (low confidence) — https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/mongodb.html · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers · also: https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/connectors/mongodb.html

## Facts and statements

- [statement] For a replacement consumer, persist restart state and make event handling idempotent. The driver specification illustrates persisting the current change and resume token for restart and assigns idempotence to the application; Debezium documents replay of already emitted events after a crash before offsets are recorded. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/change-streams/change-streams.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers · also: https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/connectors/mongodb.html, https://dev.to/deyanp/use-change-streams-instead-of-traditional-outbox-or-distributed-transactions-cdb, https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/mongodb.html
- [statement] Meltwater describes an application-hosted change-stream watcher that filters operation types, invokes event-relay logic, and sends events through SNS/SQS to consumers. Its engineering account recommends putting longer processing into a queue outside the stream handler. This is one documented replacement architecture, not a performance guarantee for another workload. (low confidence) — https://underthehood.meltwater.com/blog/2026/03/30/building-event-driven-systems-with-mongodb-change-streams/ · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers
- [statement] Translate managed and native document-image configuration separately. Atlas Document Preimage adds `fullDocumentBeforeChange` for events other than inserts; its documented managed support starts at MongoDB 4.4+ on non-sharded clusters and 5.3 on sharded clusters, including a sharding upgrade boundary of 5.3. The native manual introduces document pre- and post-images in MongoDB 6.0: enable `changeStreamPreAndPostImages` on the collection, then request `fullDocumentBeforeChange` as `required` or `whenAvailable`. Images are unavailable if they were not enabled at the event or have been removed by retention. The managed version floor is not evidence of native image support on earlier server releases. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/database-triggers.md · keywords: Atlas Trigger replacement with change-stream consumers · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/changeStreams.md
